chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna said:

I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man entered and asked him about a man who has sexual relations with a woman unlawfully (zina), can he marry her? He said, 'Yes, and her mother and her daughter.'
ai.seo_question: Does zina make a woman permanently forbidden for marriage to the man who had intercourse with her?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that *zina* (sexual intercourse) does not establish a permanent marital prohibition (*mahramiyyah*) akin to lineage or nursing, thereby permitting a man to marry the woman he had relations with, as well as her mother and daughter. This ruling distinguishes the temporary nature of the act from the structural bonds of kinship, a key point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding the scope of forbidden degrees of marriage.
